claims.text: Direct ab initio molecular-dynamics thermodynamic integration can be replaced by thermodynamic integration driven by a machine-learned interatomic potential.
A machine-learned interatomic potential trained on DFT data can accurately reproduce DFT-calculated interatomic interactions for refractory alloys.
The proposed method enables accurate high-throughput predictions of melting properties for high-melting refractory alloys.
Constant-pressure simulations around the melting point can be used to calculate the free energies of both the solid and liquid phases.
Local atomic structure and chemical disorder are relevant structural features of refractory alloys for modeling their melting behavior.
A DFT-trained machine-learning potential can capture the energetics of both solid and liquid phases.
Thermodynamic integration with the machine-learning potential yields free-energy curves for the solid and liquid phases.
The crossing of the solid and liquid free-energy curves determines the melting temperature.
Entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at melting can be obtained from the machine-learning-potential thermodynamic-integration calculations.
The machine-learning-enhanced method will achieve accuracy comparable to full ab initio molecular-dynamics thermodynamic integration.
The machine-learning-enhanced method will reduce computational cost enough to permit high-throughput screening.
Conventional DFT free-energy calculations using ab initio molecular-dynamics thermodynamic integration are computationally expensive.
Extreme anharmonicity may reduce the accuracy of the proposed method.
Inadequate sampling of relevant solid and liquid configurations in the training set may reduce the accuracy of the proposed method.
The error margins and transferability of the method across refractory-alloy compositions have not yet been established.
